content: Severe pelvic pain, nausea, vomiting, and weight gain may occur. Hypertension has been reported. Ovarian enlargement and abdominal cramps are possible. Depression and emotional instability may develop. Fever and pain, including breast tenderness and hot flashes, have been observed. Ovarian disorders, such as cysts or pain, may occur. Abdominal enlargement and pain, as well as nausea, vomiting, and weight gain, are potential side effects. Uterine spasms and vaginal discharge, bleeding, or spotting may be experienced. Injection site reactions have been reported. Post-retrieval pain is a known complication. Atelectasis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) have been documented. Thromboembolic events and anaphylaxis are rare but serious risks. Following pregnancy, complications such as spontaneous abortion, ectopic pregnancy, premature labor, postpartum fever, and congenital abnormalities may occur. Use during pregnancy may cause fetal harm. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. Elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels may indicate primary ovarian failure. Uncontrolled non-gonadal endocrinopathies, such as thyroid, adrenal, or pituitary disorders, are contraindications. Sex hormone-dependent tumors of the reproductive tract and accessory organs are contraindications. Tumors of the pituitary gland or hypothalamus are contraindications. Abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin is a contraindication. Ovarian cysts or enlargement of unknown origin, not due to polycystic ovary syndrome, are contraindications. This treatment should only be administered by physicians with extensive experience in managing fertility disorders. Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) has been reported. OHSS is distinct from uncomplicated ovarian enlargement and can progress rapidly to a serious medical condition. It is characterized by a dramatic increase in vascular permeability, leading to rapid fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity, thorax, and potentially the pericardium. The lowest effective dose should be used to minimize abnormal ovarian enlargement. If the ovaries are enlarged on the last day of therapy, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) should not be administered due to the risk of OHSS. Pulmonary and vascular complications, such as atelectasis and ARDS, may occur. Ovarian torsion has been reported following gonadotropin treatment. Multi-fetal gestation and births have been reported with all gonadotropin therapies. The incidence of congenital malformations after some assisted reproductive technologies (ART), specifically in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), may be slightly higher than after spontaneous conception, likely due to parental characteristics. Infertile women undergoing ART often have tubal abnormalities, which may increase the incidence of ectopic pregnancy. An increased incidence of spontaneous abortion and ovarian neoplasms has been observed, though causality has not been established. Pregnancy Category X: This treatment is contraindicated during pregnancy. It is not known if the drug is excreted in breast milk; therefore, it should be avoided in breastfeeding women.
